subject: Rehearsal: BYO Key Ceremony + Operator Minimums for Private Deploy
messages:
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2025-05-06T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: BYO key ceremony rehearsal request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for agreeing to run a dry-run of the BYO key ceremony before our private deployment cutover. Procurement asked that we confirm a few constraints: the ceremony should not require any permanent operator accounts on our side, there needs to be verifiable telemetry (audit logs) sent to our SIEM, and the rehearsal should include one forced-rotation scenario.

Can you share a proposed checklist and rough timeline (90–120 minute window is ideal for our ops folks)? Also confirm whether the KMS/HSM interaction will use a wrapped-KEK handshake or an ephemeral PKI assertion for the initial transfer.

Regards,
Alice Wong
Security Lead, Acme Analytics

Attachments: none
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BYO key ceremony rehearsal request

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass rehearsal plan (ceremony-simulation-plan.pdf) and an operator-minimums spreadsheet that lists the roles we propose to include during the dry-run. Summary answers up front:

- Handshake model: We will use a wrapped-KEK model for the rehearsal (HSM on your side wraps an exported DEK under your KEK; Redwood verifies wrap via attestation).
- Operator accounts: The rehearsal will use short-lived operator sessions created by Redwood’s operator-bridge; no long-lived credentials are necessary on your operator hosts.
- Telemetry: Audit events will be forwarded to both our internal logging and optionally pushed (syslog/HTTPS) to your SIEM; see the telemetry section in the attached playbook.
- Forced rotation: We propose a staged rotation scenario where one operator intentionally fails to participate, triggering quorum-based fallback and automated rewrap.

Proposed timeline (90 minutes):
1) 0-20m: Context, roles, and network connectivity checks
2) 20-50m: Attestation and initial KEK wrap exchange
3) 50-75m: Import + activation, small sample signing test, telemetry verification
4) 75-90m: Forced-rotation failure test and recovery walkthrough

Please confirm attendee list and whether your HSM supports the PKCS#11-derived attestation we reference (we included a short compatibility table in the PDF).

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ceremony-simulation-plan.pdf, operator-minimums-v1.xlsx, networking-playbook-snippets.txt
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-06T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BYO key ceremony rehearsal request

Alice / Soojin —

I reviewed the operator-minimums sheet. A couple of clarifications from an operator-control perspective:
- Minimum operator count: our recommended quorum for the rehearsal is 3 operators (2 active + 1 observer). This demonstrates split custody without introducing unnecessary personnel.
- Operator capabilities: during rehearsal each operator will have an ephemeral session token restricted to the ceremony namespace; no ability to list other tenants or export wrapping keys.
- Network isolation: rehearsal will execute over a dedicated pre-provisioned peering link (VPC peering or private interconnect). We will not enable public egress during the ceremony.

Action: Kimberly will prepare a short runbook snippet for the operator bridge to ensure the ephemeral sessions are minted with MFA enforced.

Kimberly Park
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2025-05-07T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BYO key ceremony rehearsal request

Thanks — that all sounds good. A couple of vendor-side notes before the rehearsal:
- Our HSM (vendor: Fortina HSM 3U) supports PKCS#11 but we do not have the attestation shim enabled by default; we will enable it for the test window.
- Procurement asks that any toggles that grant temporary operator access be limited to a pre-agreed maintenance window and that a DocuSign approval link be included in the event log.

We have scheduled the rehearsal for 2025-05-08 14:00 PT. Our ops team will attend. Please confirm final runbook location and the expected syslog endpoint for telemetry.

Thanks,
Alice
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-analytics.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-08T07:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BYO key ceremony rehearsal request

Alice — quick confirmations for the rehearsal tomorrow:
- Runbook: https://redwood-inference.internal/docs/byok-rehearsal-checklist (read-only link shared with Acme ops)
- Syslog/Telemetry endpoint: https://logs.acme-analytics.com/ingest (HTTPS with token-based auth); we will also mirror a copy to your SIEM via signed webhooks.
- DocuSign: I added a one-click approval stub to the runbook and enabled it for the window only; all DocuSign actions will be recorded in the audit trail.

Ben — can you validate the network snippets in the playbook (firewall rules / allowed CIDR / TCP ports) and confirm the peering config is in place?

Tessa Morgan
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme-analytics.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-08T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BYO key ceremony rehearsal request

All —

Network check completed and peering validated. Notes from my side:
- Peering type: dedicated private interconnect between Acme VPC and Redwood staging VPC; MTU and BGP sessions are up.
- Firewall: allowed TCP 443 for telemetry endpoint, TCP 1512 for PKCS#11-over-TLS (vendor-specific proxy), and ephemeral UDP/500 for the attestation handshake (vendor uses it for nonce exchange). See networking-playbook-snippets.txt.
- Fail-open scenario: the rehearsal will simulate a broken operator (we will drop its session at step 75m); routing will prefer the Redwood secondary KEK-rewrap path which uses our internal vault for ephemeral caching for 10 minutes. We logged the planned time and will include evidence in the audit bundle.

One ask: Kimberly, please ensure the ephemeral operator token expiry is set to 15 minutes for the test. If we need longer for debugging we can extend but document the extension in the runbook.

Ben Carter
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
